transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22 14:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Recording: podcast-style roundtable (for marketing)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Isabel Tran (Redwood PM), Nora Patel (Sentinel CEO), Marcus Lee (Sentinel Head of ML), Jana Ruiz (Sentinel Head of Eng), Ethan Cole (Sentinel Product Marketing)

Summary:
High-level customer marketing conversation focused on Sentinel's migration to Redwood Inference for real-time scoring and chat features. Discussed business outcomes (cost per inference, latency improvements), deployment modes used (Dedicated + Private VPC), highlights for a customer-facing case study, and next steps for technical validation and editorial approvals. Recording is slightly conversational; some side chatter and overlapping talk since this is a roundtable recording.

Topics covered:
- Why Sentinel chose Redwood (latency, cost predictability, private deploy)
- Measured improvements post-migration (p50/p95 latency, TCO)
- Integration story: rolling canary, KV cache behavior, model variant routing
- Security/compliance notes (SSO, audit logs, KMS)
- Marketing assets and testimonial approvals

Partial action notes (for show prep):
- We'll include a short quote from Nora on ROI and one from Marcus on performance.
- Technical appendix will be attached to marketing asset (links to perf spreadsheet and logs).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, welcome. Thanks for joining the Redwood x Sentinel roundtable. Uh, quick note, we'll be recording, um, with the intention of a short podcast clip and a case study. Sound good?
[00:10] Nora Patel: Yep, that's great. Happy to share — thanks for having us.
[00:14] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. We've got, uh, some numbers ready if you want them called out.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Perfect, perfect. Maybe start with a quick 30-second intros, and then we can go into the migration story. Nora, want to kick us off from the business side?
[00:28] Nora Patel: Sure. So, um, Sentinel's goal was to reduce inference cost and, and improve latency for our real-time fraud scoring. Prior to Redwood we were on CloudEndpoint's managed endpoints and we saw cost creep and higher p95s during peak windows. We needed a partner that could do private deployments and give us more predictable in voice — invoice? — predictable unit economics.
[00:48] (laughter)
[00:50] Nora Patel: Yeah invoice, sorry. Predictable invoices, yes.
[00:54] Marcus Lee: And from an engineering POV we wanted better KV cache behavior and more consistent batching. Our models are heavy context, so the KV cache reduced repeated compute for prefixing. On CloudEndpoint we hit a lot of cold-cache penalties during churn. With Redwood Dedicated and the caching policies, our p50 dropped about 30% and p95 around 20, rough ballpark.
[01:19] Jana Ruiz: To add — our on-call volume for inference-related timeouts dropped significantly. We used the Dedicated pools and then the Private VPC for sensitive traffic. The rollouts were pretty smooth — canary to 10%, 25%, then full — Redwood's routing and automatic fallback helped during a recent hardware node OOS.
[01:38] Liam Ortiz: Quick clarifying Q — when you say 30% p50 improvement, is that at 512 tokens or average token length?
[01:45] Marcus Lee: Good call. That was at our average payload, which is about 420 tokens per request. We did tests at 256 and 1024 too; the gains were larger at 256 but the production mix is mid-range.
[01:56] Isabel Tran: Marcus, did you guys enable quantization or use a different model variant in production?
[02:02] Marcus Lee: We used a 4-bit quantized variant for the lower-cost tier on non-critical paths and kept the higher-precision model for the safety checks. Redwood's Optimize suggestions actually recommended the quant profile for certain routes which saved us about 18% on token cost.
[02:17] Ethan Cole: That's the kind of number we want to front in the case study, Marcus. Any color you can give about the team reaction or time-to-value?
[02:24] Nora Patel: Time-to-value was... um, surprisingly quick. We started with a 4-week pilot — the Redwood SEs helped with the perf harness. By week six we were running canaries in prod. Our finance team saw month-over-month unit cost drop and that sold the execs.
[02:39] Maya Chen: Nice. There's always that exec buy-in moment. For the recording, would you be comfortable with us quoting 'month-over-month cost reduction of ~X%'? Or prefer a neutral phrasing?
[02:48] Nora Patel: We can share percentages but I'd like to confirm them with Marcus first, um, so let's flag that as a follow-up.
[02:55] Marcus Lee: I'll share the benchmark sheet, yes.
[02:58] (pause, mouse clicks)
[03:02] Jana Ruiz: Also worth calling out security — Redwood Private gave us KMS integration and audit logs that matched our compliance checklists. That was a hard requirement for procurement. The onboarding checklist itemized SSO/SAML and RBAC which made procurement green-light faster.
[03:17] Liam Ortiz: Great, procurement speed is a key story — do you know which audit standards you were looking to satisfy?
[03:22] Jana Ruiz: SOC 2 plus some ISO bits — our internal auditors wanted consistent retention of request-level traces for 90 days. Redwood's console and tracing hooks made that feasible without building it ourselves.
[03:34] Ethan Cole: That procurement story is gold for marketing, but we also want to humanize it — what's the one challenge that surprised you during migration?
[03:41] Nora Patel: Hmm, honestly it was mostly around traffic shaping and fallbacks. Our initial traffic profile had bursty peaks, and we hadn't tuned autoscale policies properly. Redwood's SE team suggested a burst cap and smarter routing to cheaper variants during non-critical windows. That was a key tweak.
[03:57] Liam Ortiz: When you tuned autoscale, you moved to a config with a steady baseline and a limited burst, right?
[04:02] Marcus Lee: Yeah, steady baseline for the 90th percentile day and burst for known campaign spikes. We also turned on prefix caching for conversational flows which saved tokens at the cost of a bit more memory.
[04:15] Maya Chen: For the audience, can you describe a concrete customer scenario where latency mattered?
[04:19] Nora Patel: Sure — during checkout fraud checks we need sub-250ms for the fraud call to avoid blocking UX. Pre-Redwood we occasionally spiked to 400ms at p95 which caused dropped conversions. After the migration our checkout p95 was consistently under 230ms in primary region.
[04:35] (muted background noise, slight crosstalk)
[04:40] Isabel Tran: That is a great stat. Marcus, you mentioned a perf spreadsheet — will that have the regional breakdowns and cost per million tokens?
[04:47] Marcus Lee: Yes, it'll have region, model variant, p50/p95, and effective cost per 1M tokens. I also have a small section on observed cold-cache events per day.
[04:58] Ethan Cole: For the case study, we also need a short quote around the team's experience. Nora, are you okay with a 1-2 sentence executive quote? Something like "Redwood helped us cut inference costs and stabilize latency so we could focus on product" — I'll send a draft.
[05:12] Nora Patel: Fine to draft, yes, just let me see it before publishing.
[05:16] Maya Chen: Great. Quick logistical notes — we may edit audio for clarity; we'll send the transcript for approval before publishing. Any objections?
[05:24] Jana Ruiz: No objections, just tag us in edits.
[05:27] (short laughter)
[05:30] Liam Ortiz: One tech point I want to ask — Marcus, did you run any A/B on model variants with Redwood's rollout API? Did you see any quality regressions?
[05:39] Marcus Lee: We did a small A/B on a quantized variant for lower severity checks. The quality delta was within acceptable bounds for those routes. Redwood's evaluation hooks made comparing outputs easier; we logged per-prompt regression metrics and set alerts.
[05:54] Isabel Tran: How long did it take you to set up the eval hooks?
[05:57] Marcus Lee: About a week to wire them into our CI and run the first 10k prompts. After that it was automated.
[06:04] Ethan Cole: This is great content. Two practical asks: one, we want a short engineer-to-engineer sidebar to publish as a companion blog with Marcus's notes; two, a three-sentence executive blurb. Marcus, Nora, are you comfortable with both?
[06:19] Marcus Lee: Yes to the engineering notes.
[06:21] Nora Patel: Exec blurb ok, send draft.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Awesome. Any concerns about competitor mention — do we need to avoid naming CloudEndpoint in the public piece?
[06:30] Ethan Cole: We can mention 'previous provider' if legal's nervous. We'll route the piece through both sides' legal reviews.
[06:37] (short pause)
[06:40] Nora Patel: One other small note: when you quote numbers please attribute them as 'Sentinel internal benchmark' so it's clear.
[06:47] Maya Chen: Noted.
[06:49] (transition sound, brief chuckle)
[06:52] Liam Ortiz: Switching gears slightly — any interesting anecdotes about developer experience? Jana?
[06:57] Jana Ruiz: Our SREs appreciated the rollout controls and the trace hooks. Also the console token-level cost breakdown is actually helpful — it stopped a bunch of finger-pointing across teams.
[07:09] Marcus Lee: And the ability to pin model versions per route was useful for gradual rollouts; we could run safety checks on a mirrored route before enabling traffic.
[07:19] Maya Chen: That's a nice tangible detail.
[07:22] Nora Patel: I think we should close with a one-liner about recommendation: would you recommend Redwood to other teams, Marcus?
[07:30] Marcus Lee: Short answer: yes. It gave us predictable latency, lower effective cost, and a path to private deployment without re-architecting our stack.
[07:40] Nora Patel: From the exec side, yes — it accelerated our launch and the procurement friction was lower than expected.
[07:47] Maya Chen: Awesome. Ok last bit — we'll capture these quotes and follow up with the action items. Thanks everyone for the candor and time. We'll send the draft assets and the checklist.
[07:58] Ethan Cole: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[08:01] (meeting wind-down, off-record chatter about next week)

Note: Recording contains several small overlaps and filler words which were left in to preserve natural tone. Links referenced during the call: perf spreadsheet (internal link: https://redwood.ai/links/sentinel-perf-spreadsheet), draft testimonial doc (internal link: https://redwood.ai/links/sentinel-testimonial-draft), marketing asset brief (https://redwood.ai/links/sentinel-marketing-brief).

End of transcript.
